rows.label: Value generated per dollar donated to GiveDirectly's unconditional cash transfer program
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency: GiveWell's sheet used 0.0033545 units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly here. The site values cash with one shared benchmark for every model (The cash benchmark, under Data), the same figure that turns this model's multiple of cash back into units of value: where the sheet divides by it to make its multiple, the benchmark cancels in our view, so our units of value are the sheet's before it divided by cash. The evaluator view keeps 0.0033545.

Adjustment to account for developmental benefits (long-term income increases) (#VALUE!), at your discount rate and values
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. The sheet's figure is development effects as a share of the value of the deaths averted, at GiveWell's values: children's income as adults from about 10 years on, discounted at 4%, valued at 1/ln 2, against its weight on a death. Typed in as a number, it ignored your discount rate and the income slider, and grew with the weight on a life. Our view rescales it the way AMF's and SMC's own income rows work: the present value of those years at your rate over the same at 4%, times the income slider over 1/ln 2, divided by the weight on a life (the value of deaths it is set against already carries it). At the defaults it is the sheet's figure; the evaluator view keeps it.

Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years. It is the site's shared cash benchmark (The cash benchmark, under Data), the one figure every model's multiple of cash is turned into units of value with.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs that mostly buy and hand out goods (nets, drugs, supplements, vaccines, water treatment): staff pay is a small part of the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Delivery staff are mostly hired locally at local rates, so the gap is small. Our judgment.

Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.
